arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Klausner stated that Kentucky retirement eligibility relies on twenty years of service or age fifty-five.
He argued that age is not a negative concept in this context.
He cited Justice White's view that all retirement plans distinguish based on age.
Justice Breyer questioned the factual basis of the pension calculation differences between workers with ten and twenty years of service.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Kentucky sets retirement eligibility based on twenty years of service or age fifty-five. The state argues age is a standard factor in all retirement plans. The EEOC contends Kentucky uses age to disadvantage older disabled employees. The Court must decide if this specific calculation method violates federal law.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines how states calculate disability pensions. It determines whether age can serve as a factor in these calculations. The outcome affects the financial security of disabled public employees nationwide.
